title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Santhosh Rao
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching has improved throughput but several production workloads showed unfair queueing and request starvation when load spikes and heterogeneous priorities mix. This PR introduces scheduler tuning and safety knobs to reduce starvation, improve fairness across priority classes, and bound latency via timeouts.

What changed (summary):
- Introduced a priority-aware fair queue with aging: requests are enqueued in per-priority queues and gain an aging score that increases with wait time, allowing lower-priority requests to get scheduled if they've waited beyond a threshold.
- Added max_wait_time and per-request timeout propagation: the scheduler tracks per-request enqueue times and emits a Timeout signal (and cancels inflight token allocation) if a request exceeds configured max_wait_time. This prevents unbounded queuing and improves backpressure behavior.
- Bounded batch formation latency: new config continuous_batcher.scheduler.max_batching_delay_ms ensures the batcher will force-create a batch after the delay even if target batch size not reached.
- Fairness policy selector: a runtime flag continuous_batcher.scheduler.policy (round_robin | weighted_fair | aging_fair) with weighted_fair default; the new aging_fair hybrid is enabled behind feature flag and used in the integration test harness.
- Metrics & tracing: added queue_length_by_priority, avg_wait_ms_by_priority, timeout_count, batch_formed_latency_ms histograms; added tracing spans for enqueue/dequeue/batch_build to help SRE debugging.
- Unit and integration tests: deterministic scheduler tests, simulated workload bench, and end-to-end smoke test under load.
- Small docs & config changes: documented tuning knobs and recommended defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.

Design notes and risks:
- Aging increases complexity but avoids starvation observed in mixed-latency workloads (short-low-priority mix). We cap aging influence to avoid priority inversion where low-priority always preempts high-priority.
- Timeouts allow early rejection/backpressure to callers. Default max_wait_time is conservative (200ms) and can be increased per-customer. Customers on Dedicated with high throughput can tune down max_batching_delay_ms to reduce p99 latency.
- This is opt-in behind the feature flag for now; we will enable cluster-wide after a canary and 48h monitoring window.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Synthetic benchmark simulating a 60/30/10 split high/medium/low priority clients shows 12% improvement in p95 fairness measure and a 28% reduction in timeout tail events compared to the previous scheduler under bursty load. Details in commits.
- CI: unit tests, linters, and integration suite pass after fixing a race in the batch builder.

Related: linear ENG-1423 (scheduler fairness), ENG-1489 (continuous-batcher timeouts), incident SUP-824 (production starved small requests during 2024-11-02 outage).

release_notes: Improve continuous batcher scheduling: new fairness policy with aging, queueing timeouts, and tunable max batching delay. Reduces starvation and improves fairness under bursty mixed-priority workloads. Config knobs: continuous_batcher.scheduler.policy, continuous_batcher.scheduler.max_wait_time_ms, continuous_batcher.scheduler.max_batching_delay_ms.
canary_plan: Deploy to canary pool (5% traffic) for 48h with additional metrics dashboards for queue_length_by_priority, avg_wait_ms_by_priority, and timeout_count. If timeout_count spikes > 1% of requests or p99 latency regresses > 10% for high priority, rollback and investigate.
